title: Visibility-Sensitive Command Streaming for Native GGML FPGA Inference
title_zh: 面向原生 GGML FPGA 推理的可见性感知命令流式传输
hook: At low batch, a native GGML trace may contain a small set of host-visible or stateful boundaries and a much larger device-only data-plane bulk, so treating every call as equally observable can manufacture most of the XRT launch cost. Visibility-Sensitive Trace Compression predicts that preserving the boundary set while streaming the bulk as exact device bytecode lowers p50 decode latency on Gemma 3 1B F16 U280 runs without changing the captured native result or explicit-error behavior.
abstract_draft: Low-batch LLM inference on an FPGA can be limited less by arithmetic than by repeatedly crossing the host-to-device launch boundary for a native GGML execution trace. Existing FPGA designs such as LlamaF [openalex:W4405909140] improve model-specific compute mappings, but retain a control plane in which many original runtime calls remain separately dispatched or are replaced only by static, model-shaped groups. We propose Visibility-Sensitive Trace Compression (VSTC), a native-runtime control-plane method that records a visibility-sensitivity ticket for every original GGML call, preserves host-visible or stateful boundaries, and streams only eligible device-only runs as exact patchable bytecode on a resident interpreter. The contribution is a per-call admission protocol that makes command compression conditional on observed reads, aliases, state, consumer structure, allocation identity, scratch requirements, and explicit-error behavior rather than on a fixed operator class. VSTC is falsified if, on Gemma 3 1B F16 U280 runs, admitting more eligible template entries does not reduce p50/p95 prefill or decode latency relative to a naive resident descriptor engine, or if forcing those same entries back to individual completion does not restore that latency. If the premise holds, the method removes avoidable XRT submissions while retaining bytewise logits and native explicit-error traces.

motivation.problem_framing:
The central bottleneck is a control-plane mismatch in native, low-batch FPGA inference: a GGML trace contains calls whose results must remain observable to the host or participate in mutable state, alongside a larger data-plane bulk whose intermediate completions are not semantically required. Treating both groups as equally observable turns a semantic precaution into repeated XRT launch traffic. The primary instance is llama.cpp running Gemma 3 1B F16 on a U280, but the issue is structural for native tensor runtimes whose call graph and buffer identities are only known at execution time.

Prior FPGA LLM work improves the data plane rather than representing this runtime distinction. LlamaF [openalex:W4405909140] uses model-specific matrix concatenations and W8A8 kernels while keeping attention control and KV-cache work on the processing system; Big PE [openalex:W4416342314] increases systolic-array density for prompt processing; and XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1] improves mixed-precision MAC utilization. These approaches can reduce computation cost, but none supplies a per-original-call decision record that establishes when native completion, allocation identity, alias behavior, state, and explicit errors may be preserved while launch submission is compressed.
motivation.why_now: Recent FPGA LLM work makes the remaining control-plane gap more visible: Big PE [openalex:W4416342314] and XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1] each push the compute datapath toward higher density or better datatype utilization, so host dispatch becomes a more consequential fraction of low-batch latency rather than an incidental overhead. At the same time, llama.cpp exposes a stable native GGML call stream and XRT provides the command and completion interfaces needed to capture it, while U280-class boards can host a small resident interpreter without replacing the installed F16 kernels. These conditions make it practical to test a runtime representation change directly instead of inferring its benefit from a model-specific accelerator redesign.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: Big PE [openalex:W4416342314] co-designs a denser 4x4 8-bit coarse-grained systolic cell for TinyStories prompt processing on PCIe-based FPGAs.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not preserve a native F16 GGML call stream through a per-call visibility partition or reduce launch submissions while retaining each original call's completion and error semantics.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Its optimization unit is a compute-array mapping, which has no runtime representation of host reads, aliases, state, or consumer visibility from which safe command admission can be decided.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: LlamaF [openalex:W4405909140] accelerates Llama2 with model-specific Wq/Wk/Wv and W1/W3 concatenations plus two W8A8 GQMV kernels, while retaining attention control and KV-cache handling on the processing system.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not construct patchable exact templates from the live GGML trace or give every original call an individually surfaced completion after eligibility is established.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: Static matrix grouping is defined before execution and therefore cannot encode the dynamic host-observation, alias, state, scratch, allocation, and explicit-error facts required for native-runtime command compression.

why_prior_stopped.what_they_did: XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1] builds a datatype-adaptive mixed-precision MAC that shares mantissa products to improve FPGA DSP utilization.
why_prior_stopped.what_they_did_not_do: It does not alter the host command representation or suppress repeated XRT submissions when the same F16 data-plane kernels are retained.
why_prior_stopped.structural_reason_they_stopped: A MAC microarchitecture has no control-plane mechanism for deciding whether a runtime call may defer host-visible materialization without changing native behavior.

motivation.what_changes_when_gap_closes: Closing this gap would let a native llama.cpp backend retain its original tensor allocation and explicit-error contract while avoiding per-call host launches for device-only portions of prefill and decode. That creates a reusable runtime path across model traces instead of requiring each new model to be recast into a bespoke matrix schedule, complementing the data-plane advances in LlamaF [openalex:W4405909140] and XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1]. It also makes a concrete systems claim available: latency improvements can be attributed to a measured reduction in semantically unnecessary submissions, rather than to an inseparable accelerator redesign.

core_claim: VSTC lowers low-batch native GGML FPGA inference latency by admitting only calls proven device-only by a per-call visibility ticket into exact streamed templates while preserving the original host-visible completion and error behavior.

sub_claims.statement: A per-original-call visibility-sensitivity ticket can separate calls that require host-observable completion from calls whose intermediate device results can remain internal without changing the captured native contract.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the bottleneck that makes a native runtime conservatively pay an XRT launch for every GGML call.

sub_claims.statement: Patchable exact bytecode templates with per-call completion identities can stream eligible bulk work on a resident interpreter without replacing the installed F16 kernels or caller tensor allocations.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the gap between model-specific static fusion and a reusable representation for a live native GGML trace.

sub_claims.statement: The admission fraction rho and an otherwise-identical forced-individual-completion control distinguish the benefit of visibility-sensitive compression from generic resident-engine overhead reduction.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the causal-identification gap in the latency claim by tying the claimed mechanism to an intervention on admission.

method_flow.high_level_pipeline: VSTC first observes the native GGML/XRT execution stream and records a ticket for each original call rather than assuming that calls of the same operator type have the same safety conditions. It evaluates those tickets to retain host-visible or stateful calls as H boundaries and to admit only device-only calls as B entries. Consecutive B entries are encoded as exact, patchable device bytecode and interpreted by a resident engine, while H calls keep individually surfaced completion and explicit-error behavior. The backend then audits the resulting execution against the native trace and relates latency changes to rho, the fraction of baseline submissions represented by admitted B entries.

steps.title: Capture native call tickets
steps.what_changes: Instrument each original GGML/XRT call to emit a ticket containing host-read, alias, state, unique-consumer, original-allocation, scratch, and explicit-error facts together with its original call identity.
steps.why_this_step: The heterogeneous-decomposition decision must be made from runtime semantics rather than from a static operator name or model-specific matrix group.
steps.input: Native llama.cpp GGML call stream, tensor metadata, and XRT submission/completion events.

steps.title: Partition observable boundaries
steps.what_changes: Evaluate the admission predicate on each ticket, retaining H calls that require host materialization or stateful handling and marking only safe device-only calls as B entries.
steps.why_this_step: The partition prevents command compression from crossing the visibility, alias, state, allocation, scratch, or error conditions that define the native contract.
steps.output: H/B partition with a recorded reason for every denied B admission.

steps.title: Build exact B templates
steps.what_changes: Encode contiguous admitted B entries as patchable exact device bytecode with their original bindings, call identities, and completion slots rather than replacing them with an approximate fused operator.
steps.why_this_step: Exact templates retain the installed F16 kernels and caller allocation semantics while eliminating repeated host-side reconstruction of device-only submissions.
steps.input: Admitted B entries and original GGML/XRT argument bindings from S2.
steps.output: Patchable B-template records plus per-original-call completion metadata.

steps.title: Stream bulk and surface boundaries
steps.what_changes: Run B-template records through the resident interpreter while dispatching H boundaries with individually surfaced completion states and propagating the original explicit-error behavior.
steps.why_this_step: This realizes the claimed launch reduction without turning the resident engine into a generic asynchronous scheduler that hides native runtime observability.
steps.input: B-template records, H boundaries, and the original execution order.
steps.output: Native-compatible logits, tensor effects, completion states, and explicit-error trace.

steps.title: Audit equivalence and admission
steps.what_changes: Check bytewise logits and explicit-error traces against the native backend, optionally force full observation, and compute rho together with XRT-submission and p50/p95 latency measurements.
steps.why_this_step: The full-observation oracle and forced B-denial control test whether any speedup comes from visibility-sensitive admission rather than from an unmeasured interpreter or changed kernel path.
steps.input: Execution outputs from S4 and matched native, resident-engine, and admission-disabled runs.
steps.output: Equivalence verdict, admission fraction rho, submission counts, and latency evidence.

method_flow.design_reasoning_echo: VSTC treats semantic visibility, not arithmetic type, as the source of heterogeneity in a native trace. The design therefore records facts at the granularity at which the caller can observe behavior, applies a conservative admission predicate, and compresses only the residual device-only bulk as exact templates. This differs from fixed operator fusion or model-specific matrix concatenation because each B decision is justified by the current call's read, alias, state, consumer, allocation, scratch, and error conditions. Per-call completion identities and the full-observation oracle keep the representation accountable to the native execution contract, while the forced-denial control makes the H/B partition itself experimentally distinguishable from merely installing a resident interpreter.

plain_motivation_en:
The bottleneck is a control-plane mismatch in native, low-batch FPGA inference. A GGML trace can include calls whose results must stay visible to the host or take part in mutable state, alongside a larger device-side bulk whose intermediate completions do not need to be surfaced. Treating both groups as equally observable turns a semantic safeguard into repeated XRT launch traffic. The main example is llama.cpp running Gemma 3 1B F16 on a U280, but the issue is structural for native tensor runtimes whose call graph and buffer identities are only known at execution time.

Recent FPGA LLM work makes the remaining control-plane gap easier to see. Big PE [openalex:W4416342314] and XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1] both push the compute path toward higher density or better datatype use, so host dispatch becomes a larger share of low-batch latency instead of a minor overhead. At the same time, llama.cpp exposes a stable native GGML call stream, XRT exposes the command and completion interfaces needed to capture it, and U280-class boards can host a small resident interpreter without replacing the installed F16 kernels. These conditions make it practical to test a runtime-representation change directly rather than infer its value from a model-specific accelerator redesign.

Prior work stops short for a structural reason. Big PE [openalex:W4416342314] changes the compute array mapping, which has no runtime record of host reads, aliases, state, or consumer visibility. LlamaF [openalex:W4405909140] uses model-specific matrix grouping and keeps attention control and KV-cache work on the processing system, but it does not build patchable exact templates from the live GGML trace or give each original call an individually surfaced completion after eligibility is decided. XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1] improves MAC utilization, but a MAC microarchitecture cannot decide whether a runtime call may defer host-visible materialization without changing native behavior.

If this gap closes, a native llama.cpp backend can keep its original tensor allocation and explicit-error contract while avoiding per-call host launches for the device-only parts of prefill and decode. That gives one reusable runtime path across traces instead of requiring each new model to be recast into a bespoke matrix schedule, and it makes the latency claim easier to attribute to a measured reduction in unnecessary submissions rather than to a bundled accelerator redesign.
plain_motivation_zh:
核心瓶颈是原生、低 batch FPGA 推理里的控制面不匹配。一个 GGML trace 里可能既有必须让主机看见结果、或者会参与可变状态的调用，也有一大段只在设备侧流动、并不需要逐个显式完成的 bulk。把这两类调用都当成同样可见，就会把一种语义上的保守处理变成反复的 XRT 启动开销。这里的主要例子是 llama.cpp 在 U280 上运行 Gemma 3 1B F16，但这个问题对所有只在执行时才知道调用图和缓冲区身份的原生张量运行时都是结构性的。

最近的 FPGA LLM 工作让剩下的控制面空缺更明显了。Big PE [openalex:W4416342314] 和 XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1] 都是在把计算路径推向更高密度或更好的数据类型利用，所以在低 batch 场景里，主机调度会比以前占更大比例的延迟，而不再只是一个小开销。与此同时，llama.cpp 提供了稳定的原生 GGML 调用流，XRT 提供了捕获它所需的命令和完成接口，U280 级板卡也可以容纳一个小型 resident interpreter，而不必替换已安装的 F16 kernels。这样的条件使得直接测试一种运行时表示的变化变得可行，而不是只能从某个模型专用加速器改造去间接推断它的价值。

前人的工作停在结构性原因上。Big PE [openalex:W4416342314] 改的是计算阵列映射，而这种映射里没有主机读取、别名、状态或消费者可见性的运行时记录。LlamaF [openalex:W4405909140] 用的是模型专用的矩阵分组，并把 attention control 和 KV-cache 工作留在 processing system 上，但它没有从真实 GGML trace 里构造可 patch 的 exact templates，也没有在资格判定后给每个原始调用单独暴露完成。XtraMAC [arxiv:2605.06052v1] 提高的是 MAC 利用率，但一个 MAC 微架构本身并不能决定某个运行时调用是否可以延后主机可见的 materialization，而又不改变原生行为。

如果这个空缺被补上，原生 llama.cpp backend 就能在保留原始 tensor allocation 和 explicit-error contract 的同时，避开 prefill 和 decode 中设备侧部分的逐调用主机启动。这样就得到了一条能在不同 trace 之间复用的运行时路径，而不用把每个新模型都重新改写成一套专门的 matrix schedule；同时，延迟提升也更容易归因于可测量的无谓 submission 减少，而不是归因于一个打包在一起的加速器重设计。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 给每个原始 GGML/XRT 调用打一个 ticket，记录 host-read、alias、state、unique-consumer、original-allocation、scratch 和 explicit-error 这些事实，以及这个调用的原始身份。输入：native llama.cpp GGML 调用流、tensor metadata 和 XRT submission/completion 事件。输出：按顺序排列的每调用可见性感知 ticket trace。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 压缩决策必须来自运行中的程序到底能观察到什么，而不能只看 operator 名称，或只看一个静态的模型分组。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 对每个 ticket 计算 admission predicate，保留那些需要 host materialization 或有 stateful handling 的 H 调用，只把安全的 device-only 调用标成 B entries。输入：来自 S1 的有序 ticket trace。输出：H/B partition，并且为每个被拒绝的 B admission 记录原因。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 这个 partition 不能跨过定义原生 contract 的 visibility、alias、state、allocation、scratch 或 error 条件。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 把连续被准入的 B entries 编成可 patch 的 exact device bytecode，并保留它们原始的 bindings、call identity 和 completion slots，而不是把它们替换成一个近似的 fused operator。输入：来自 S2 的已准入 B entries 和原始 GGML/XRT argument bindings。输出：可 patch 的 B-template records，以及每个原始调用对应的 completion metadata。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: exact templates 保留了已安装的 F16 kernels 和调用方的 allocation 语义，同时去掉了反复在 host 侧重建 device-only submissions 的开销。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 把 B-template records 送进 resident interpreter，同时让 H boundaries 以单独可见的 completion state 发出，并传播原始的 explicit-error 行为。输入：B-template records、H boundaries 和原始执行顺序。输出：与 native 兼容的 logits、tensor effects、completion states 和 explicit-error trace。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 这样才能实现声称的 launch reduction，同时又不把 resident engine 变成一个隐藏 native runtime observability 的通用异步调度器。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 把 bytewise logits 和 explicit-error traces 与 native backend 对齐检查，必要时强制 full observation，并计算 rho 以及 XRT-submission 和 p50/p95 latency measurements。输入：S4 的执行输出，以及匹配的 native、resident-engine 和 admission-disabled runs。输出：equivalence verdict、admission fraction rho、submission counts 和 latency evidence。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: full-observation oracle 和 forced B-denial control 用来检验任何加速到底是不是来自 visibility-sensitive admission，而不是来自一个没有被单独测量的 interpreter，或者来自一条改过的 kernel path。

plain_method_modules_en.purpose_oneline: Record what each native call exposes, then split the trace into host-visible boundaries and safe device-only bulk.
Turn eligible bulk into exact streamed templates and run them while keeping boundary behavior visible.
Check that the streamed path still matches native outputs and measure whether admission actually helps.

plain_method_modules_zh.purpose_oneline: 先记录每个原生调用能暴露什么，再把 trace 分成主机可见的边界和安全的设备侧 bulk。
把可准入的 bulk 变成可精确流式执行的 templates，并在保持边界行为可见的同时运行它们。
检查流式路径是否仍与原生输出一致，并衡量 admission 是否真的带来收益。

falsification_prediction: Implement the exact supported Gemma 3 1B F16 path in llama.cpp on the AMD Alveo U280, run pp512 and tg128 with fixed 512-token prompts from the wikitext-2-raw-v1 test split, and compare native per-XRT dispatch, the naive resident descriptor engine, and VSTC while checking bytewise logits and explicit-error traces. If VSTC is correct, p50 and p95 tg128 per-token latency and pp512 latency decrease as the named load-bearing variable rho, the fraction of baseline XRT submissions represented by admitted B-template entries, rises above zero; XRT run submissions should fall in the same direction without a new CPU fallback. The negative control overrides the B admission result for exactly the otherwise eligible calls, forcing individual host-visible completion and materialization while retaining the same kernels and inputs; if p50/p95 latency does not return toward the naive resident-engine baseline, the claimed visibility-sensitivity mechanism is falsified rather than merely unmeasured. A secondary full-observation oracle can force every produced tensor to be checked against the native backend after each call, testing whether the capture premise rather than template execution caused any mismatch. Add control arms on the same Gemma U280 workloads and existing latency/error metrics: an all-eligible homogeneous template slice comparing the single-record and multi-record interpreter, and a mixed trace with B admission forced off while the same engine remains active, so the interpreter and H/B partition effects are independently identifiable.
compute_budget: 0.5 80GB-class GPU-day for trace-analysis and regression tooling plus 30 U280 board-days for HLS builds, hardware debug, and the full pp512/tg128 campaign; $0 paid API cost because the campaign uses local llama.cpp, Gemma 3 1B F16, XRT, and wikitext-2-raw-v1.
what_step_was_missed: LlamaF would have needed to construct a per-original-GGML-call visibility-sensitivity ticket trace, including captured host-read, alias, state, and one-consumer conditions, then interpret eligible exact templates with individually surfaced completion states; concatenating fixed matrix groups cannot construct that dynamic native command representation.

compute.rationale: GPU line ≈ 0.5 vs 150 GPU-day (0%) → feasible; API line ≈ $0 vs $10000 (0%) → feasible. Overall (worse line) → feasible.

data.rationale: llama.cpp, the wikitext-2-raw-v1 prompts, and the supported Gemma 3 1B F16 inference inputs are accessible for the stated workload; a publicly downloadable GGUF checkpoint with the same GGML operation coverage can substitute during trace development if the exact weights are unavailable.

theoretical.rationale: The contribution is an executable native-runtime representation and equivalence check rather than a theorem claim, so no unproven theoretical prerequisite is required for the proposed result.

engineering.rationale: The binding cost is U280 HLS/XRT integration and debugging of exact bytecode, per-call completion, alias handling, and regression capture, although the proposal reuses existing llama.cpp and F16 kernels rather than requiring a new accelerator datapath.

falsification.rationale: The named Gemma/U280 pp512 and tg128 workloads, native and resident-engine controls, bytewise logits, explicit-error traces, XRT submission counts, and forced B-denial intervention can all be implemented with the existing runtime and board tooling.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Abstract-only inference: Big PE constructs a denser 4x4 8-bit systolic compute cell for TinyStories prompt processing, whereas VSTC constructs a visibility-sensitivity partition plus per-original-call completion protocol that compresses the native F16 command stream across prefill and decode without changing the caller's tensor allocation.

LlamaF constructs model-specific Wq/Wk/Wv and W1/W3 matrix concatenations with two W8A8 GQMV kernels while retaining attention control and KV cache on the processing system; VSTC instead constructs patchable exact templates from the runtime GGML call stream and makes per-call eligibility depend on observed visibility, alias, state, and scratch facts.

Abstract-only inference: XtraMAC constructs a datatype-adaptive MAC with shared mantissa products, whereas VSTC constructs a control-plane representation that removes repeated host launch submissions even when every installed data-plane kernel remains the same F16 operation.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Paper-pointed threat: semanticscholar:32c402c2cab23299458f1819bc823c79d7219e9c (collision_hits). CDA-GNN is the closest retrieved competitor because it reports a U280 asynchronous accelerator that exploits dependency chains to avoid synchronization. Its dependency chains are predetermined for GNN state propagation, however, whereas VSTC's claim depends on dynamically capturing per-GGML-call host observation, alias, state, unique-consumer, original-allocation, and explicit-error conditions before a B template is admitted. CDA-GNN therefore motivates a strong comparison but does not establish the candidate's exact native-runtime mechanism.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: The defense is anchored in `core_mechanism_steps`: VSTC captures per-original-GGML-call host observation, alias, state, unique-consumer, allocation, scratch, and explicit-error conditions before any B template is admitted, whereas CDA-GNN's retrieved dependency chains are predetermined for GNN state propagation. The `falsification_prediction` further keeps a naive resident descriptor engine and an admission-disabled control, so a benefit cannot be attributed merely to having an asynchronous U280 engine.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Un-retrieved mechanism family flagged by the audit (parametric knowledge, not in the retrieved pool): Dynamic command-graph and deferred-execution runtimes; query vocabulary: dynamic CUDA Graphs capture, runtime command buffer batching, XRT command-buffer dependency scheduling. — novelty vs this family is UNVERIFIED; run a targeted scoop-check on that vocabulary before investing.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: A targeted scoop-check must establish whether dynamic command-graph, deferred-execution, or XRT command-buffer systems already preserve the same per-call host observation, alias, state, allocation, completion, and explicit-error contract while streaming exact native-runtime templates. VSTC's delta survives only if that full native-semantic admission protocol is absent or materially different.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Gap-closure reject-check borderline on gap 1 (C04 (Decompose for Differentiated Treatment)): Presenting a sensitivity or redundancy proxy as the novelty invites the verdict that it rediscovers known mixed-precision or low-rank results unless it is sharply differentiated from the obvious prior; Skipping any analysis of why the heterogeneity exists — the data or value distribution that drives the partition — makes the technical novelty and the potential impact impossible to assess.; Bolting together established components (distillation plus pruning plus calibration) without an error bound or artifact specific to the new setting reads as incremental even when the target applicatio
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: The candidate does not use a numerical sensitivity proxy to rediscover mixed precision or low rank; its `core_mechanism_steps` classify runtime observability conditions and preserve original call identities. The ticket predicate, full-observation oracle, and forced B-denial branch in `falsification_prediction` expose why this heterogeneity exists and test the partition against a fixed interpreter and unchanged kernels.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Anti-pattern matched: audit_decomp_operator. Required mitigation: The operator's expressivity gain must be demonstrated on homogeneous data (where decomposition is unnecessary), and the decomposition's separate effect must be demonstrated on heterogeneous data with the operator held fixed. Each leg's contribution must be independently identifiable.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses.response: The `falsification_prediction` directly supplies the required two-leg mitigation: an all-eligible homogeneous slice compares the single-record and multi-record interpreter, while a mixed trace forces B admission off with the same engine active.
